A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same PepHAR research work, with readable text, equations, figures, tables, and complete Appendices A–H. Text and rendered-page comparisons support reliable matching throughout.

before.justification: v2 reports original computational results for peptide binder design and scaffold generation, including component ablations and further empirical analyses in Appendix G.

after.justification: v3 retains the work's original binder-design and scaffold-generation experiments, ablations, and Appendix G analyses.

M1.justification: The founding, autoregressive extension, and correction stages, Algorithm 1, network components, losses, and sampling procedures are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same PepBDB/Q-BioLip complexes for binder design and hotspot-conditioned scaffold generation. The GPCR case study in Appendix G.4 is also unchanged.

E2.justification: RFDiffusion, ProteinGenerator, PepFlow, and PepGLAD remain the comparators in both main tasks and the supplementary hotspot-count comparison, with identical membership in Tables 1, 2, and 7.

E3.justification: The dataset split, pocket definition, evaluation metrics, 64 generated peptides per target, and training and sampling settings in Section 5 and Appendices E–F are unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 3's component ablations, hotspot-count analyses, cumulative-error analysis, GPCR case study, and secondary-structure analysis are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Figure 3's RMSD boxplots and Appendix F's averaging practice are unchanged. No independent-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests are added or revised.

E6.justification: All main and appendix result tables and empirical figures retain identical values and findings. For example, PepHAR with K=3 retains RMSD values of 2.68 Å in Table 1 and 2.15 Å in Table 2.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, objectives, sampling equations, backbone-reconstruction derivations, and von Mises formulas are identical. Figure 1's atom-label correction does not revise the formal definitions or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims concerning hotspot-driven peptide generation, geometric constraints, and binder-design and scaffold-generation performance.

C2.justification: Interpretations of the quality/diversity tradeoff, autoregressive error accumulation, baseline behavior, and limited strand generation in Section 5.3 and Appendix G are unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendices E–F retain the same implementation, hardware, hyperparameter, and evaluation details. Both abstracts promise future code availability at the same repository; the wording edit does not change the stated access status.

R1.justification: Section 2, Appendix H, and the reference list are unchanged. No cited works or substantive positioning relative to prior research are added or removed.

P1.justification: v3 changes 'Source code' to 'The source code' in the abstract, updates the arXiv version/date stamp, and adds acknowledgement of Wuxi Research Institute of Applied Technologies, Tsinghua University, Grant 20242001120. The narrative and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 1 replaces three carbonyl-carbon labels Cβ with C and slightly adjusts panel framing. The expanded acknowledgement changes spacing on page 11; other figures, tables, and appendix layouts are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 corrects Figure 1's misleading Cβ labels to C, aligning the peptide-bond schematic with Appendix B's carbonyl-carbon description. This modestly improves explanatory accuracy, while the methods, empirical evidence, formal derivations, and reproducibility information remain unchanged.
